item.name: 1 User Login With Mobile Number (Send OTP)

request.description:
## User Login With Mobile Number (Send OTP)

Initiates the user login flow by sending a One-Time Password (OTP) to the specified mobile number via SMS. This is the first step in the two-step mobile authentication process.

---

### Endpoint

`POST {{baseURL}}/auth/send-otp`

---

### Authentication

None required.

---

### Request Body

**Content-Type:** `application/json`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mobile_number` | `string` | ✅ Required | The user's registered mobile number to which the OTP will be sent. |

**Example:**
```json
{
    "mobile_number": "8291598930"
}
```

---

### Response

#### 200 OK — OTP Sent Successfully

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "message": "OTP Sent successfully",
  "data": {
    "expires_in_seconds": 600,
    "channel": "sms"
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `success` | `boolean` | Indicates whether the OTP was sent successfully. |
| `message` | `string` | A human-readable status message. |
| `data.expires_in_seconds` | `number` | The validity duration of the OTP in seconds (e.g. `600` = 10 minutes). |
| `data.channel` | `string` | The delivery channel used to send the OTP (e.g. `"sms"`). |

---

### Notes

- The OTP expires **10 minutes** (600 seconds) after it is sent.
- OTPs are delivered via **SMS** to the provided mobile number.
- After receiving the OTP, use the **Verify OTP** endpoint to complete authentication.
- Ensure the mobile number is registered in the system before calling this endpoint.

response.name: 1 User Login With Mobile Number (Send OTP)

request.description:
## User Verification With OTP (Verify OTP)

Verifies a user's identity by validating the OTP (One-Time Password) sent to their registered mobile number. On successful verification, the server returns a JWT auth token along with the user's profile details.

---

### Endpoint

`POST {{baseURL}}/auth/verify-otp`

---

### Request Body

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mobile_number` | string | Yes | The user's registered mobile number. |
| `code` | string | Yes | The OTP code received on the mobile number. |

**Example:**

``` json
{
    "mobile_number": "8291598930",
    "code": "1234"
}

 ```

---

### Response

**Success (200 OK)**

``` json
{
    "success": true,
    "message": "Login successfull",
    "data": {
        "token": "<JWT_TOKEN>",
        "user": {
            "id": "439",
            "name": "Krushang",
            "email": "user@example.com",
            "username": null,
            "two_fac_auth": false,
            "role": "user",
            "developer_id": "353",
            "project_ids": ["206", "208", "226", "231"]
        }
    }
}

 ```

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `success` | boolean | Indicates whether the request was successful. |
| `message` | string | Human-readable status message. |
| `data.token` | string | JWT token to be used for authenticating subsequent requests. |
| `data.user.id` | string | Unique identifier of the user. |
| `data.user.name` | string | Display name of the user. |
| `data.user.email` | string | Email address of the user. |
| `data.user.role` | string | Role assigned to the user (e.g., `user`). |
| `data.user.developer_id` | string | Associated developer account ID. |
| `data.user.project_ids` | array | List of project IDs the user has access to. |
| `data.user.two_fac_auth` | boolean | Whether two-factor authentication is enabled. |

---

### Post-Response Script

After a successful response, the `authToken` environment variable is automatically set to the returned JWT token. This token is then used by subsequent requests in the collection for authenticated API calls.

---

### Notes

- The `authToken` environment variable must be set before calling any authenticated endpoints. This request handles that automatically on success.
    
- Ensure the correct `baseURL` environment variable is configured before sending this request.
    
- The `authToken` is also known as the `masterToken` in the application and is mainly used for most of the APIs in this collection.
    
- The list of APIs that use `authToken` / `masterToken` are
    

1. "3 Get All Project Details For a User"
    
2. "4 Get Project Specific Token"
    
3. "5 Get all notifications"
    
4. "6 Get Profile Details Of User"
    
5. "7 Get Specific Details Of a Project For a User"
    
6. "8 Get List Of Towers For a Project"
    
7. "10 List of Users for a Developer"
    
8. "11 List of User for a particular Project"
